ABSTRACT: Two methods, designed primarily for applications in diversity-oriented synthesis (DOS), are introduced. The first is a
Cu−H-catalyzed multicomponent process that involves a nitrile and a trisubstituted allenyl boronate. The first set of products are
homoallylic α-secondary NH -amines, containing a trisubstituted alkenyl boronate, formed with >98% enantiospecificity, in up to
>98:2 dr and as a single alkene isomer (>98% Z). The second method is eficient and diastereoselective triflic anhydride-mediated
conversion of an unsaturated azapane-amide, generated from modification of the products of the foregoing catalytic process to
azabicyclooctanes (ABCOs). The ABCOs contain a bridged enamine moiety and a trisubstituted alkene, which can be functionalized
chemo- and stereoselectively. Accordingly, natural product-like rigid bicyclic frameworks can be obtained wherein four diferent
fragments can be installed in space in a controllable fashion.

In planning these studies, the inspiration came from
azapenes (AZPs; Scheme 1a), exemplified by benazepril<sup>4</sup> and
the related azabicyclooctanes (ABCOs), such as crinine,<sup>5</sup>
lyconadin A<sup>6</sup> and himgaline.<sup>7</sup> We wanted to develop methods
that can be used to generate stereochemically defined
multifunctional compounds that, while possessing the same
AZP or ABCO core framework, would be clearly distinct from
any extant natural products. The first step would be a catalytic
multicomponent reaction that afords a multifunctional core
platform. A related transformation, reported previously, is
promoted by a Cu−B(pin) and a Cu−H catalyst (Scheme 1b)<sup>8</sup>
and involves a nitrile and a monosubstituted allene (→ Cu-
allyl-1 → ketim-1 → amin-1). Here, we would have a chiral
trisubstituted allenyl boronate (Scheme 1c) and a Cu−H
catalyst<sup>9</sup> would be involved in both C−C bond formation (→
Z-ketim-2) and ketimine reduction (→ Z-amin-2). Because
the catalytic reaction would deliver a Z-trisubstituted alkenyl
boronate (vs a 1,1-disubstituted boronate in the earlier report),
we would be able to access AZPs via Z-amin-2 (azp; Scheme
1c). Ensuing amide formation (amid) and cyclization through
a keteniminium salt (ketenim)<sup>10</sup> by a Bischler−Napieralski-
type cyclization would deliver ABCOs bearing a rarely
encountered<sup>11</sup> bridgehead enamine and a fourth stereodefined
moiety (enam-1−4).

with allenes bearing a single substituent, where a Cu−H
complex adds to the less substituted site, the situation is more
complex with a trisubstituted allenyl boronate. Although Cu−
allyl-2 formation would be favored based on electronic
stabilization,<sup>12</sup> addition to the less substituted C�C would
be less sterically demanding. It was also unclear to what degree
stabilization of electron density<sup>12</sup> by the boryl unit would
impact the allyl-metal’s nucleophilicity, and whether it would

transformation that, as far as we know, has no precedent, or a
less substituted Cu−allyl complex. There would be no internal

ketimine would be more exposed and susceptible to a second
